title: Disk Manager & Buffer Manager
overview:
In this project you will implement the lowest two layers of the EduDBMS storage stack: the **Disk Manager** and the **Buffer Manager**.

A disk-oriented DBMS stores data in files on persistent storage (SSD or HDD). Data is organized in fixed-size units called **pages** (4 KB each). The DBMS cannot operate on disk pages directly — it must first copy them into memory. The **Buffer Manager** acts as a cache between the execution engine and disk, keeping frequently accessed pages in a fixed-size memory pool and evicting cold pages using a replacement policy.

Your implementation will handle raw page I/O, a buffer pool with pin/unpin semantics, and an LRU (Least Recently Used) eviction policy.

tasks.title: Disk Manager
tasks.description: The `DiskManager` class manages raw page-level I/O to a single database file. Each page occupies exactly `DB_PAGE_SIZE` (4096) bytes at file offset `page_id * DB_PAGE_SIZE`.

functions.name: ReadPage(page_id_t page_id, char* data)
functions.description: Read the contents of the specified page from disk into the `data` buffer. Seek to the correct file offset (`page_id * DB_PAGE_SIZE`) and read exactly `DB_PAGE_SIZE` bytes. If the page is beyond the current file size, zero-fill the buffer.
hints: Use `seekg()` to position the read pointer.
Use `read()` to copy bytes into `data`.
Check `page_id >= num_pages_` for the zero-fill case.

functions.name: WritePage(page_id_t page_id, const char* data)
functions.description: Write `DB_PAGE_SIZE` bytes from `data` to the specified page on disk. Seek to the correct offset and flush the write to ensure durability.
hints: Use `seekp()` to position the write pointer.
Call `flush()` after writing to ensure data reaches disk.
Update `num_pages_` if writing beyond the current extent.

functions.name: AllocatePage() → page_id_t
functions.description: Allocate a new page by returning the current `num_pages_` value and incrementing it. The actual disk space will be allocated on the first `WritePage` call.
hints: This is a simple counter increment.

tasks.title: LRU Replacer
tasks.description:
The `LRUReplacer` tracks which buffer pool frames are candidates for eviction. Only unpinned frames (pin_count == 0) are tracked. When a frame is pinned, it is removed from the replacer. When unpinned, it is added to the back of an LRU list. `Victim()` evicts the least-recently-used frame from the front of the list.

Internally, use a doubly-linked list (`std::list`) for O(1) removal and a hash map (`std::unordered_map`) mapping frame_id to list iterator for O(1) lookup.

functions.name: Victim(frame_id_t* frame_id) → bool
functions.description: Remove the least-recently-used frame from the replacer. Set `*frame_id` to the evicted frame's ID. Return `true` if a victim was found, `false` if the replacer is empty.
hints: The victim is at `lru_list_.front()`.
Remove from both `lru_list_` and `lru_map_`.

functions.name: Pin(frame_id_t frame_id)
functions.description: Remove the given frame from the replacer, making it non-evictable. If the frame is not in the replacer, do nothing.
hints: Check `lru_map_.find(frame_id)` first.
Erase from both map and list.

functions.name: Unpin(frame_id_t frame_id)
functions.description: Add the given frame to the replacer, making it evictable. If the frame is already in the replacer, do nothing (do not move it).
hints: Guard against duplicates with `lru_map_.count()`.
Use `push_back` and `std::prev(lru_list_.end())` to record the iterator.

tasks.title: Buffer Manager
tasks.description:
The `BufferManager` manages a fixed-size pool of in-memory page frames. It loads pages from disk on demand via `FetchPage`, writes dirty pages back on eviction or explicit flush, and uses the `LRUReplacer` for eviction decisions.

**Key concepts:**
- **Frame**: a slot in the buffer pool (indexed 0 to pool_size-1)
- **Page**: a `DB_PAGE_SIZE` block on disk (indexed by page_id)
- **Page Table** (`page_table_`): maps page_id → frame_id for pages currently in the pool
- **Free List** (`free_list_`): frames not yet assigned to any page
- **Pin Count**: number of threads/operations currently using the page. A page with pin_count > 0 cannot be evicted.

functions.name: FetchPage(page_id_t page_id) → Page*
functions.description:
Fetch a page into the buffer pool. If the page is already in the pool, increment its pin count and return it. Otherwise, find a free frame (from `free_list_`) or evict one via the replacer. If the evicted frame is dirty, flush it to disk first. Read the requested page from disk into the frame, update `page_table_`, and return the page with pin_count = 1.

Return `nullptr` if all frames are pinned and no eviction is possible.
hints: Step 1: Check `page_table_` for a cache hit.
Step 2: On miss, try `free_list_` first, then `replacer_.Victim()`.
Step 3: If victim is dirty, call `disk_manager_->WritePage()`.
Step 4: Update `page_table_`, call `disk_manager_->ReadPage()`.
Step 5: Set page metadata (page_id, pin_count=1, dirty=false).

functions.name: UnpinPage(page_id_t page_id, bool is_dirty) → bool
functions.description: Decrease a page's pin count. If `is_dirty` is true, mark the page as dirty. When pin_count reaches 0, add the frame to the replacer (making it evictable). Return `false` if the page is not in the pool or already has pin_count 0.
hints: Look up the frame via `page_table_`.
Decrement pin_count. If it reaches 0, call `replacer_.Unpin(frame_id)`.
Set the dirty flag with OR semantics (don't clear it if already dirty).

functions.name: FlushPage(page_id_t page_id) → bool
functions.description: Write a page's data to disk regardless of its dirty flag. Clear the dirty flag after writing. Return `false` if the page is not in the pool.
hints: Call `disk_manager_->WritePage(page_id, page.GetData())`.
Set `page.SetDirty(false)` after flushing.

functions.name: NewPage() → Page*
functions.description:
Allocate a new page in both the buffer pool and on disk. Find a free frame (or evict). Then call `disk_manager_->AllocatePage()` to get a new page_id. Initialize the frame and return it with pin_count = 1.

**Important:** Acquire the frame before calling `AllocatePage()` to avoid leaking page_ids if eviction fails.
hints: Step 1: Find a frame (free_list_ or victim).
Step 2: If victim is dirty, flush it.
Step 3: Call `AllocatePage()` to get the new page_id.
Step 4: Reset frame, set page_id, pin_count=1.

functions.name: FlushAllPages()
functions.description: Write every dirty page in the pool to disk and clear its dirty flag. Clean pages need no work.
hints: Iterate through `page_table_`.
For each dirty page, call `disk_manager_->WritePage()` and clear the flag.

functions.name: DeletePage(page_id_t page_id) → bool
functions.description: Remove a page from the buffer pool and hand its frame back to the free list. Return `false` if the page is still pinned; return `true` if it was removed, and also if it was never in the pool.
hints: Look it up in `page_table_`. Not there means nothing to do — return `true`.
A `pin_count` above 0 means someone is still using it — return `false`.
Drop it from `page_table_`, reset the frame, push the frame onto `free_list_`.
Take the frame out of the replacer with `Pin()`.

breakdown.covers: Page read/write, allocate, persistence across instances
Victim selection, pin/unpin ordering, edge cases
Fetch, cache hit, eviction, dirty flush, all-pinned

testing.note: These tests are the actual grading tests.
testing.platforms: macOS or Linux, on either Intel or ARM. On Windows, build inside WSL: a native Windows toolchain is refused, because the reference libraries these downloads carry are built for macOS and Linux only.

hints: Start with `DiskManager` — it has no dependencies and the simplest logic.
Test `LRUReplacer` independently before integrating with `BufferManager`.
In `FetchPage`, handle the cache-hit case first (it's simpler).
Use `memset(data, 0, DB_PAGE_SIZE)` when you need to zero-fill a page.
Remember that `UnpinPage` uses OR semantics for the dirty flag: a page that was marked dirty earlier should stay dirty even if unpinned with `is_dirty=false`.
Draw out the frame/page_table/free_list state transitions on paper before coding.

submission.where: Upload the archive to PLMS (https://plms.postech.ac.kr) under Project #1 before the deadline. Submissions sent by email, or left anywhere else, are not collected.
submission.note: Keep the original directory layout inside the archive (src/…), so the files drop straight back into the project tree. Submit only the files you edited: no build/ directory, no compiled objects, no reference libraries.
